summary: The note covers a Friday ASX open expected lower after Wall Street fell on Thursday as rising Treasury yields and slightly hotter-than-expected inflation data raised fears the Fed will keep rates high. It details US market moves, bond yields, oil prices tied to fighting in Gaza, and corporate news such as Delta, Ford and the UAW strike. It also lists Australian share winners and losers and notes Atlassian's acquisition of Loom.
one_line: Hotter US inflation and rising bond yields sent Wall Street lower and pointed to a weaker ASX open, with oil, Fed worries and company news in focus.
key_facts: The S&P 500 was 0.7 per cent lower in afternoon trading on Thursday and on track to break a four-day winning streak, its longest since August.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 204 points, or 0.6 per cent, as of 3pm Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 0.8 per cent lower.
Weak results from an auction of 30-year Treasury bonds sent yields higher; the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.7 per cent from 4.56 per cent late Wednesday.
The two-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.06 per cent from 4.99 per cent.
The Federal Reserve announces its next interest rate move on November 1; Seema Shah of Principal Asset Management called the inflation data "reassuringly uneventful".
Benchmark US crude slipped US58¢ to settle at $US82.91, while Brent crude rose US18¢ to $US86 a barrel, with prices shaky after the latest fighting in Gaza.
Delta Air Lines fell 2.3 per cent despite stronger-than-expected summer profit and encouraging holiday bookings.
Ford Motors slumped 1.9 per cent after 8700 workers walked out at a Ford truck plant in Louisville, Kentucky, as the United Auto Workers escalated its strike.
On the ASX, Harvey Norman fell 4.4 per cent as it went ex-dividend, weighing on consumer discretionary (down 1 per cent).
Resmed extended losses after RBC downgraded it, while Newcrest stepped up after investors approved its merger with Newmont.
Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo and UnitedHealth Group were due to report on Friday, starting a season that could mark a return to profit growth after three straight quarters of declines.
Atlassian announced it was acquiring Loom, a US-based enterprise video chat and screen recording pioneer; co-founder Mike Cannon-Brookes commented on the deal.
Rising 10-year yields have pushed mortgage rates to their highest levels since the turn of the millennium.
